statement: A curated library of foundational treatises in operating systems, algorithms, information theory, compiler design, and physical optics.

currentlyReading.title: The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 1: Fundamental Algorithms
currentlyReading.author: Donald E. Knuth
currentlyReading.userReview: The standard of mathematical rigor and algorithmic analysis. Data structures are the core foundation; everything else is secondary.
currentlyReading.quoteSnippet: Premature optimization is the root of all evil (or at least most of it) in programming.

currentlyReading.title: The C Programming Language
currentlyReading.author: Brian W. Kernighan & Dennis M. Ritchie
currentlyReading.userReview: Concise, precise, and without superfluous padding. The finest programming book ever written.
currentlyReading.quoteSnippet: C is not a big language, and it is not well served by a big book.

currentlyReading.title: The Design of the UNIX Operating System
currentlyReading.author: Maurice J. Bach
currentlyReading.userReview: The book that made Unix internal mechanics clear to an entire generation of systems programmers.
currentlyReading.quoteSnippet: The file system is a tree-structured hierarchy of files.

currentlyReading.title: The Mathematical Theory of Communication
currentlyReading.author: Claude E. Shannon & Warren Weaver
currentlyReading.userReview: Founded the entire field of digital communication. Absolute clarity of thought.
currentlyReading.quoteSnippet: The fundamental problem of communication is that of reproducing at one point either exactly or approximately a message selected at another point.

currentlyReading.title: The Camera (The Ansel Adams Photography Series 1)
currentlyReading.author: Ansel Adams
currentlyReading.userReview: Rigorous optical understanding coupled with profound aesthetic discipline.
currentlyReading.quoteSnippet: You don't take a photograph, you make it.
